subject: Nimbus Health — commit uplift & throughput runway discussion
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodai.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@nimbushealth.com>, Tom Gallagher <tgallagher@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodai.com>
Date: 2027-05-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Nimbus Health — commit uplift & throughput runway discussion

Hi Elena / Tom,

Great talking yesterday — appreciate the transparency on projected usage as you roll the triage assistant into three additional hospitals. Per our notes, you're expecting sustained QPS to grow from ~120 qps today to ~420 qps by Dec 2027 with average request sizes increasing from ~450 tokens to ~700 tokens as richer context is added. I've attached a forecast workbook and a draft MAA with proposed term changes.

High-level recommendation (to consider ahead of renewal):
- Reserved pool: increase from 8 -> 24 GPUs (A10G-equivalent profile) to meet steady-state throughput and maintain our 95th-pct latency target at 350ms.
- Burst capacity: keep 6 GPU burst headroom for scheduled peak windows (nightly batch inference + morning clinics).
- Throughput guarantee: commit to a minimum of 380 qps sustained with autoscale buffer and fallback to compatible model (quantized variant) if utilization exceeds 90%.
- Term: 18-month commitment with quarterly throughput reviews and a one-time right to upsize at month 6 with pre-agreed uplift pricing.

Attached: nimbus-forecast-q3q4-2027.xlsx (workbook), redwood-maa-draft-v2.pdf. See the throughput-tab for per-endpoint token/CPS breakdown.

Ask: Can you confirm the Dec go-live window for the inpatient rollout and whether procurement needs an updated quote that includes the burst pool and an SLA addendum? If procurement is ready we can turn these numbers into a formal amendment for signatures.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
M: (415) 555-0127

From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@nimbushealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodai.com>
Date: 2027-05-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Nimbus Health — commit uplift & throughput runway discussion

Karthik — thanks for the summary and the workbook. Quick questions: 

1) That 24 GPU recommendation feels like a big jump — can you share the per-model QPS assumptions and how much of that is headroom vs baseline?
2) For burst capacity, do you bill for the full reserved GPU or just consumed GPU-hours? We need to reconcile this with our budget model.
3) We also need an explicit latency SLO for the triage endpoint (95th pct). Is 350ms measured server-side or end-to-end (including networking + LB)?

Procurement (cc'd) will want the pricing line-items broken out (base reserved, burst reserved, overage rate, and discount tiers). Can you send a short amendment we can circulate?

Best,
Elena
Director of Product Operations | Nimbus Health

> Great talking yesterday — appreciate the transparency on projected usage as you roll the triage assistant into three additional hospitals.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodai.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@nimbushealth.com>, procurement@nimbushealth.com
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodai.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodai.com>
Date: 2027-05-19T08:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Nimbus Health — commit uplift & throughput runway discussion

Elena — thanks, great questions. Answers inline and added a short appendix in the workbook.

1) Per-model assumptions:
- Triage classifier (small): baseline 120 qps today; projected 160 qps by Oct; 220 qps by Dec. Average token size low (30-60 tokens) so cheap to serve.
- Contextual summarizer (medium): baseline 20 qps today; projected 95 qps by Nov; 140 qps by Dec. Average token size 400-700.
- Clinical prompt generator (large): baseline 5 qps; projected 25 qps by Dec; token size 1,200 on long documents but those are batched overnight.

We modeled utilization with a 20% effective batching gain on the summarizer and a 1.8x token-per-request increase to account for richer context. The 24 GPU recommendation is to hold 90% of peak sustained demand within the reserved pool while leaving burst for exceptional windows. The workbook contains a sheet ("GPU-sim") with hourly simulated utilization over a representative 30-day period.

2) Billing model for burst: reserved GPUs are billed as part of the committed capacity. Burst capacity (the extra 6 GPUs) can be purchased as on-demand reserved add-on (hourly consumed) or as a small monthly bolt-on license. In the amendment we will show both options: (A) bolt-on reserved burst at 6 GPUs with reduced hourly rate, (B) pure on-demand at a higher overage rate. Typically customers pick (A) when they want predictable cost for scheduled peaks.

3) Latency SLO: 350ms is server-side P95 (inference time on our runtime). End-to-end targets will be higher; we recommend an E2E P95 of 450ms to account for network and LB. We can add an explicit E2E SLO to the MAA addendum with agreed measurement windows and a credit schedule.

Next steps I propose:
- I'll circulate a short amendment template with both pricing options (bolt-on burst vs on-demand) plus explicit SLO language.
- Laura / Marissa will review the E2E instrumentation and confirm the dashboard we will hand over at go-live.

Laura / Marissa — can you confirm the GPU sizing assumptions are OK and whether we should recommend a 16->24 ramp or a 12->24 phased plan for procurement planning?

Thanks,
Karthik

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodai.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodai.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodai.com>
Date: 2027-05-19T11:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Nimbus Health — commit uplift & throughput runway discussion

Karthik / Elena — quick ops check from the sizing team:

- Confirmed that the simulated workload in the workbook uses conservative kernel selection for the summarizer (quantized Llama-2-medium variant) yielding ~2.8 tokens/ms on A10G-equivalents. The "GPU-sim" tab includes a sensitivity column for quantization (no quant / int8 / int4).
- Phased recommendation: 12 GPUs reserved initially with a contractual right to add 6 GPUs at month 3 and the remaining 6 at month 6 (so 12 -> 18 -> 24). This reduces immediate cash outflow and aligns with your hospital rollout windows.
- Autoscale policy: we suggest a 85% utilization soft-threshold to trigger pre-warm flows for additional containers, with a hard 93% cap where we start traffic-shifting to the quantized fallback.

I'll attach a short CSV showing assumed QPS-to-GPU mappings by model for the amendment.

Laura
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Karthik / Laura — thanks for the clear breakdown and the phased path. Procurement reviewed the bolt-on vs on-demand options and prefers the phased reserved approach (12 -> +6 @M3 -> +6 @M6) to smooth cashflow. A few follow-ups: 

- Please send the amendment with clear line items and the quarter-by-quarter billing projection.
- We need the E2E P95 SLO language in the MAA with measurement and credit terms.
- Do you have a simple one-page runbook for failover (if we hit the hard 93% cap and the quantized fallback is in use)? That will help our SRE team sign off.

If we can get the amendment and runbook this week we can aim for procurement sign-off by 2027-06-01.

Appreciate the collaboration — Elena and I will coordinate final internal approvals.

Tom Gallagher
VP, Digital Platforms | Nimbus Health
